title: Stock arrangements and the Waltz Dream dance band
summary: Waters describes the Waltz Dream hall for Black dancers, the stock arrangements and Schoebel-type charts they played, and why a leader who wanted music played straight made him happy to jump to Miller.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Of the other bands you were playing with in Philadelphia around this period - first of all, when Driver heard you and recommended you to Charlie Miller, was that a gig with Lonnie Polk or was that just -

No, that was different, that was a gig with a, it was a dance band, I was working at the Waltz Dream - did I say Waltz Dream before? - yeah, Waltz Dream, it was a dancing hall for negroes. Lot of people would be there, see - I think it was three times a week or something like that. And we had music - see, you could buy, you could buy stock arrangements, that's when the birth of stock arrangements, you know. And you also buy semi-swing things, you know, little things by guys like, have you ever heard of a guy named Elmer Scobel?
Schoebel, I got the wrong name, yeah.
Well, I mean, I had something of - well, he was mak-, he was one of the first to listen to negro bands, or any other band that was swingin', and write it out.

You know, it was things like that, see. Then - well, as far as those popular songs, like I was saying, "See You In My Dreams", that's the one popular song I [ ], "See You In My Dreams" - you could buy the arrangements for that -
Whether they were Schoebel arrangements or -

There was more so in that period, there was more so 2 saxophones, tenor and alto. It wasn't so much 3, the 3 came up later. The 4 came up later and the 5 and like that, see. But it was, it was started with tenor and alto, you couldn't buy for 3, they didn't have it, see. Tenor and alto, and trumpet. Trombone, that's what you could buy it for. And then all you got to do is read, and it would sound OK for dancing. But it was limit, because the leader of the band himself didn't want too much solos and things, you see, that's why, see? The leader of the band himself wanted you to play the music the way it is, and it would sound OK. But it wouldn't give you enough jazz if you wanted to be a soloist, that wouldn't, it wouldn't help - you'd stale, you get stale in that particular category, you see what I mean? And that's what I was, that's what worried me - see, I'm, that's why I jumped when I had the chance to jump to Charlie, I was happy, just like a rabbit in a briar patch or somethin', I was happy to jump to that group because I could do what I wanted to. It was that type of band, see. We, we didn't, [ ] - to tell you the truth, we didn't have much music because we could fake so much.
